children: Stock index futures fell early Monday, pointing to a lower open as investors weighed developments around the artificial intelligence sector and monitored oil prices following a sharp move higher.
Now, here are 4 news stories that broke overnight to watch out for:
OpenAI rules out 2026 IPO over safety focus:

will not go public this year, calling the timing "ill-advised" given current safety and alignment challenges. "We need to be able to make decisions that are not obviously in the interest of our business and our shareholders for the responsibility of fulfilling our mission," Altman told Fortune. He indicated OpenAI and other AI companies could be nearing an agreement to address safety risks by slowing development pace. Altman has reportedly pushed advisers to target a $1 trillion valuation for any eventual public offering.
Trump dismisses AI safety slowdown warnings:

calls from tech leaders to slow AI model development, arguing that imposing restrictive guardrails would risk ceding America's technological lead to China. "We're leading China in AI. We're the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins," Trump told reporters Sunday at the Irish Open. His comments followed proposals from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, backed by OpenAI's Sam Altman and xAI's Elon Musk, to give safety measures more time to catch up with increasingly capable models. National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett described AI safety as a manageable problem, suggesting voluntary industry safeguards could provide a workable model.
Supertanker freight rates surge to record highs:

for Very Large Crude Carriers on the benchmark Middle East-to-China route hit a record of nearly $800,000 following the biggest wave of attacks on Middle East shipping since the start of the U.S.-Iran conflict. The U.S. Gulf-to-Asia run has fetched offers at a record lump-sum fee of $29.5 million, roughly $15 per barrel before war-risk premiums. Freight analysis from Kpler suggests VLCC dayrates will stay above $100,000 into next year, more than double historic levels that rarely exceeded $45,000. "There's quite a few bottlenecks all at the same time," Equinor's global head of crude trading Alex Grant said. "The market is quite stressed with all of that."
Novo Nordisk rebrands to 'Novo' amid obesity battle:

announced it will shorten its corporate name to Novo and update its logo, with its trademark bull shifting to face right. CEO Mike Doustdar is pushing to make the company leaner and more competitive as it works to regain market share in obesity treatments against Eli Lilly, which has increasingly adopted a single-name identity by dropping "Eli" from marketing materials. Novo will provide a detailed overview of its updated corporate strategy at its Capital Markets Day on September 21 in London.
